newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA GAS OIL/JET - DIESEL UP ON TRADER SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: ASIA GAS OIL/JET - DIESEL UP ON TRADER SUPPORT.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices were marginally firmer on continued buying by a western trader, traders said on Monday.
But the market was fundamentally weak, as supplies were ample, and demand from endusers, especially China remained subdued, they said.
"There's still an overhang that needs to be worked out," said a trader with a major oil company.
"There might be some demand from Philippines, but how much can they take?" said another trader.
On Monday, a western trader bought 150,000 barrels of gas oil loading August 27-31 from a major at $22.50 per barrel on a free-on-board basis.
The level of the trade was slightly higher compared to a trade done at $22.40 on Friday.
But the buying in the last week has been by just a single trader, keeping the market guessing where all the barrels were heading to.
The bearish sentiment was further aggravated by rumours that Taiwan was looking to sell two to three cargoes in its September tender.
The tender, which was issued last week, was due to close late Monday, and was for September 5-30 lifting.
Some traders said they were looking to the Indian October buy tender closing next week for direction.
But others said that in light of India's meagre diesel purchase in its September tender, they were not expecting any big buying from India for October.
The jet fuel market was similarly under pressure on limited buying interest.
Traders said that the contango of around 60 cents between August and September, was prompting some players to store jet fuel barrels, expecting improved demand as winter approaches.
"But there is plenty of jet around, and very little regional demand" said a trader.
India awarded its superior kerosene tender for September to Mobil, at seven cents per barrel over Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
The level awarded in the tender was just four cents higher from August tender award, and traders saw this to be a bearish sign.
